what: Flexible creation of baseline descriptive tables
title: Flexible creation of baseline descriptive tables
text: DescriptiveTable R package creating tables baselines descriptives (sometimes referred ‘Table 1’ epidemiological research settings). package developed maintained Real World Evidence (RWE) research group UMCU. inputs required : dataset rows equal units one groups, columns equal covariates (group identifier) metadata file defining output table; variables included, nesting counts done, information displayed, text labels variable Based inputs, DescriptivesTable() outputs baseline descriptives table: table describing, one groups, descriptive statistics cell counts, means, medians quantiles, list different covariates. tables typically used characterize covariate distribution population, describe differences covariate distributions two groups. Table shell example baseline descriptives Although multiple packages exist creating tables, package developed incorporate variety specific needs RWE, : calculation absolute standardized differences (ASDs) compare variables different types across groups (using stddiff package) calculation weighted ASDs (using, e.g., IPT weights) using custom functions Masking cell counts smaller pre-specific integer comply privacy regulations Specification different nesting structures, headings display names using flexible metadata format Wrangling large datasets using data.table

title: Flexible creation of baseline descriptive tables
text: DescriptiveTable uses metadata file specify desired output. metadata file contains one row per variable included table, order display, defines following columns: var name variable (column) input covariate dataset TF (binary, true/false, count TRUE displayed), CAT (categorical, display count percentage), NUM1 (numeric, display mean SD one row, median Q1 Q3 second) NUM2 (numeric, display median Q1 Q3 one row, min-max second). expectedCat defines category values displayed table. Can string listing category values interest, string format get <object_name> <object_name> vector global environment containing category values listed. label display name give variable. parent parent_cat defines denominator cell counts. default, parent = NA means overall table total used denominator. Otherwise parent var name must specified, corresponding parent variable category. header defines optional header string displayed variable, instance, cluster related variables displayed example variety input options specified provided package extdata folder. can see example metadata, expectedCat entry points global object called study_quarters_all. run example code, need specify objects global environment
code: # load specification of the table # "parent" variables and categories determine the denominator used to compute percentages for that variable table_metadata <- fread(   system.file('extdata/example/', 'BaselineDescriptives_metadata.csv', package = 'DescriptiveTable')) # global parameters (interact with get() in table metadata) study_quarters_all <- c("2021 Q1", "2021 Q2", "2021 Q3", "2021 Q4", "2022 Q1", "2022 Q2", "2022 Q3", "2022 Q4", "2023 Q1")

title: Flexible creation of baseline descriptive tables
text: Two additional optional inputs, can passed vectors DescriptivesTable function, note. first lookup table dictionary, maps integer values categorical variables dataset meaningful labels displayed table. example supplied second piece information can supplied vector defines variables treated missing. important remember scripts may deployed different data-access providers, may access study variables interest. instance, one DAP may access smoking behaviour, another . consistency sake, input dataset DAPs may contain column reflecting smoking study variable, filled dummy (0) values DAP variable measured. work around may load additional metadata file pass relevant information function
code: # load helper information value-labels of categorical variables label_lookup <- readRDS(   system.file("extdata/example/", "label_lookup.rds", package = "DescriptiveTable"))  label_lookup[4:9,] #>         VarName category integerVal #> 7     L_SEX_COV   Female          1 #> 8     L_SEX_COV     Male          2 #> 19 PREG_QUALITY    green          1 #> 20 PREG_QUALITY   yellow          2 #> 21 PREG_QUALITY     blue          3 #> 22 PREG_QUALITY      red          4 # settings DAP <- "TEST1"  # load helper information on what variables are expected to be missing in the DAP ExpectedMissingVars <- data.table::fread(     system.file("extdata/example/", "ExpectedMissingVariables.csv", package = "DescriptiveTable")) ExpectedMissingVars <- ExpectedMissingVars[get(DAP) %in% TRUE, VarName]
